chapter: New Orleans musicians, recordings and radio
title: New Orleans musicians in Chicago and who came to sit in
summary: Most of the best Chicago music came from New Orleans players like Pops Foster, the Dodds, Dutrey and Bechet; local and white musicians came to Dreamland after hours to learn their style.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Now, some of the best music in Chicago at that time -- and we're talking about the '20's -- was really being played by New Orleans people, wasn't it?

Absolutely. All the -- most of the music was played by the New Orleans people, because it was Louie and Joe -- what's that -- Papa -- what's the man's -- the big, the guy, not big guy, but the guy that played the -- didn't he play bass, this big man?
Pops Foster, you mean?
Yeah, Pops Foster and Johnny Dodds -- Dodds Dodge Brothers.
(Inaudible), Honore Dutrey and -- Baby Dodds
Honoré Dutrey, Bechet -- Bechet --
Lawrence? What was his name? They called him -- she said he played a very squeaky clarinet, he said.
Lawrence?
Lawrence Duhé.
Oh, yes, Lawrence Duhé, yeah. But anyhow, it --
Lil told me that there were Chicago musicians, but they didn't really swing like --

They didn't play like those New Orleans boys did. The New Orleans boys had something that the Chicago musicians couldn't get at that particular time. And I tell you what. Every musician in the area that could get to the Dreamland would be there to come to sit in with those fellows to play, to try to get their style and see what they did, you know, and especially during the after hours. After hours they'd come and sit with those New Orleans musicians.

From all downtown, from everywhere they'd come from way over on the West side. They had a Dreamland over on the West side, you know, a dance place. Well, Elgar's band -- he had a band I forget his first name -- Elgar, his musicians would come; everybody would come, all the musicians from the different places.
And, of course, all the white musicians --
By all means.

Bix Beiderbecke
Big Spiderback
Do you remember Big Spiderback at all?
Not well.
Frankie Trumbauer -- any of those people? (inaudible) the trombone.

Yeah. I don't remember them well, but I just know that all the white musicians would come in there, -- to try to get the style, the same as the white artists would come in to try to get the colored singers' styles, you know?
